chapter.v:
Send your
bread out on the surface of the water, and many days later you will find it again.

Share what
you own with seven or eight people, for you never know what disaster could happen.

When the
clouds are full they pour rain down upon the earth. Whether a tree falls to the north or to the south, it stays where it fell.

The farmer
who pays attention to the direction of the wind knows when not to sow, and by watching the clouds knows when not to reap.

Just as
you don't know how the breath of life comes to the child in its mother's womb, so you can't understand the work of God, the Creator of everything.

In the
morning, sow your seed. In the evening, don't stop. For you have no way of knowing which crop will grow well—one may be profitable, or the other—or maybe both.
chapter.heading: Before the Years Take Their Toll
chapter.v:
How sweet
it is to live in the light, to see the sun rise on another day.

May you
live for many years, and may you enjoy them all. But remember there will be many days of darkness, and all that is to come is uncertain.

Young people,
enjoy your youth! Be happy with what's good! While you're young, let your mind guide your life, and do as you think best. But remember that God will judge you for all your thoughts and actions.

So don't
let your mind worry, and avoid things that hurt your body. Even so, despite youth and enthusiasm, life is still so hard to understand!
